fragments.text: Use one supplied photograph; output portrait 3:4 with its unwarped scene filling the background.
Suspend one horizontal open book front-on at center; book edges lie at canvas x=10–90% and y=28–72%.

Place left-aligned English handwriting on the left leaf, within canvas x=22–45%, vertically centered with generous paragraph gaps.
Use faded blue-grey ink near #585D83, upright rounded unjoined letters, medium felt-tip strokes and gently irregular baselines.
Use single-storey lowercase a and g; character height approximately 2.4% and baseline spacing approximately 3.1% of full canvas height.
The sample reads exactly Two quiet shores. then One day to keep. in separate paragraphs; use supplied text for other inputs.
Place one portrait 3:4 crop from this same photograph on the right leaf, at canvas x=53–80% and y=36.5–63.5%.
Give the inset a hairline white edge and tiny rounded corners, surrounded by visible ivory paper; avoid thick instant-photo framing.
The inset may crop but must retain source geography, subjects and lighting; it contains no book and creates no recursive image.

Fit the upper photograph through restrained environment extension where necessary; never stretch, twist or redesign its principal subject.
In the lower half, reinterpret the recognizable subject and its relationships as a small isometric paper-model illustration, not photographic texture mapping.
Use a consistent axonometric view, simplified solid volumes, clean edges and a tiny cropped ground base surrounded by abundant blank paper.
Preserve defining posture, silhouette, openings and adjacency; compress minor detail rather than copying every texture or inventing a second focal point.
Describe structure with fine ink contours, restrained flat color planes, paper grain and light soft shadows.
Sample the upper photograph's identifying colors and warm-cool relationships; purify and soften them into a small coherent palette without unrelated presets.
Separate adjacent volumes using close hues and modest value changes; avoid glossy plastic rendering and candy-like saturation.
Use scale contrast, trimmed ground edges and a few tiny source-related supports to suggest a miniature exhibit; leave the surroundings spacious.
Integrate a short English title with the base or a quiet layout axis; allow one sparse number or note in slender modern type.
For this sample use THE BLUE DOOR and STUDY 01; for other inputs use supplied copy or a short observed-subject title.
